description: CLOUD INFRASTRUCTURE: servers, containers, virtualization, orchestration, deployment — a modern-region anchor. Focused member concepts sharpening the already-present (diffuse) cloud microtheory so it edge-grounds modern.

microtheory.name: cloud_infrastructure
microtheory.definition: The modern practice of running software on pools of remote, virtualized compute: servers and datacenters, containers and their orchestration, autoscaling and load-balancing, deployment and provisioning. A post-1885 computing world.

concepts.name: server
concepts.definition: A networked computer that provides a service to clients.

concepts.name: container
concepts.definition: A lightweight, isolated package of an application and its dependencies.

concepts.name: kubernetes
concepts.definition: The dominant system for orchestrating containers across a cluster.

concepts.name: virtualization
concepts.definition: Running many isolated virtual machines on one physical host.

concepts.name: deployment
concepts.definition: The act of releasing a version of software to run in an environment.

concepts.name: autoscaling
concepts.definition: Automatically adding or removing capacity as load changes.

concepts.name: load_balancer
concepts.definition: A component distributing requests across a pool of servers.

concepts.name: datacenter
concepts.definition: A facility housing the pooled servers, storage and networking of the cloud.

concepts.name: orchestration
concepts.definition: Automated coordination of the deployment, scaling and health of services.

concepts.name: microservice
concepts.definition: A small independently-deployable service, one of many composing an application.

concepts.name: vm_hypervisor
concepts.definition: The layer that creates and runs virtual machines on physical hardware.

concepts.name: provisioning
concepts.definition: Preparing and configuring infrastructure resources for use.
